newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia Irkutsk region plans $80 mln Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Russia Irkutsk region plans $80 mln Eurobond.

text.p: The Siberian region of Irkutsk plans to raise $80 million through a Eurobond issue early in 1998, regional Deputy Governor Vladimir Dvornichenko said on Thursday, adding the denomination of the bond had not been set.
"This will happen early in 1998," Dvornichenko told Reuters.
The All-Russian Bank for Regional Development is the agent for the planned issue and ING-Barings is the rating consultant of the project, he said.
Dvornichenko said the Eurobond would mainly be aimed at southeast Asian markets, such as Taiwan, Japan and South Korea.

"We think the European market will be oversupplied and we have the right to look for other markets, namely southeast Asia," he said. "We have very good neighbourly relations with them." Irkutsk has direct flights to many Asian states.
The Irkutsk region joins a long queue of Russian cities and regions, including Moscow, St Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod, eager to enter international capital markets.
Dvornichenko said the regional administration would choose a rating agency in two weeks and lead managers would be announced by May.
The region plans to use the funds to finance area investment programmes, including development of the Kovyktinskoye natural gas field.
Some Russian estimates put Kovyktinskoye's confirmed reserves at 300 billion cubic metres and unconfirmed reserves at 600 billion cubic metres.
